## Scope of this Part and interpretation

## 74.1

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.1] (1) Section I of this Part applies to the enforcement in England and Wales of judgments of foreign courts. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.1] (2) Section II applies to the enforcement in foreign countries of judgments of the High Court and of the County Court. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.1] (3) Section III applies to the enforcement of United Kingdom judgments in other parts of the United Kingdom. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.1] (4) Omitted

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.1] (4A) Omitted

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.1] (4B) Section VI applies to—

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.1] (a) the certification in England and Wales of outgoing protection measures; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.1] (b) the enforcement in England and Wales of certified protection measures from Member States of the European Union other than Denmark. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.1] (5) In this Part –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.1] (a) ‘the 1920 Act’ means the Administration of Justice Act 1920 1 ;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.1] (b) ‘the 1933 Act’ means the Foreign Judgments (Reciprocal Enforcement) Act 1933 2 ;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.1] (c) ‘the 1982 Act’ means the Civil Jurisdiction and Judgments Act 1982 3 ;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.1] (d) to (f) Omitted (g) ‘the 2005 Hague Convention’ means the Convention on Choice of Court Agreements concluded on 30th June 2005 at The Hague;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.1] (h) “the 2019 Hague Convention” means the Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Judgments in Civil or Commercial Matters concluded on 2nd July 2019 at The Hague. ## I ENFORCEMENT IN ENGLAND AND WALES OF JUDGMENTS OF FOREIGN COURTS

## Interpretation

## 74.2

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.2] (1) In this Section –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.2] (a) ‘Contracting State’ has the meaning given in section 1(3) of the 1982 Act;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.2] (b) Omitted

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.2] (c) ‘judgment’ means, subject to any other enactment, any judgment given by a foreign court or tribunal, whatever the judgment may be called, and includes

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.2] (i) a decree;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.2] (ii) an order;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.2] (iii) a decision;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.2] (iv) a writ of execution or a writ of control; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.2] (v) the determination of costs by an officer of the court;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.2] (d) ‘State of origin’, in relation to any judgment, means the State in which that judgment was given; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.2] (e) ‘writ of control’ is to be construed in accordance with section 62(4) of the Tribunals, Courts and Enforcement Act 2007;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.2] (f) ‘writ of execution’ includes—

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.2] (i) a writ of possession;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.2] (ii) a writ of delivery;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.2] (iii) a writ of sequestration;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.2] (iv) a writ of fieri facias de bonis ecclesiasticis,

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.2] and any further writ in favour of any such writs, but does not include a writ of control. ## Applications for registration

## 74.3

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.3] (1) This Section provides rules about applications under –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.3] (a) section 9 of the 1920 Act, in respect of judgments to which Part II of that Act applies;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.3] (b) section 2 of the 1933 Act, in respect of judgments to which Part I of that Act applies;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.3] (c) section 4B of the 1982 Act;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.3] for the registration of foreign judgments for enforcement in England and Wales; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.3] (d) section 4C of the 1982 Act. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.3] (2) Applications –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.3] (a) must be made to the High Court; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.3] (b) may be made without notice. ## Evidence in support

## 74.4

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (1) An application for registration of a judgment under the 1920, 1933 or 1982 Act must be supported by written evidence exhibiting –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (a) the judgment or a verified or certified or otherwise authenticated copy of it; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (b) where the judgment is not in English, a translation of it into English –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (i) certified by a notary public or other qualified person; or

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (ii) accompanied by written evidence confirming that the translation is accurate. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (2) The written evidence in support of the application must state –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (a) the name of the judgment creditor and his address for service within the jurisdiction;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (b) the name of the judgment debtor and his address or place of business, if known;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (c) the grounds on which the judgment creditor is entitled to enforce the judgment;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (d) in the case of a money judgment, the amount in respect of which it remains unsatisfied; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (e) where interest is recoverable on the judgment under the law of the State of origin –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (i) the amount of interest which has accrued up to the date of the application, or

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (ii) the rate of interest, the date from which it is recoverable, and the date on which it ceases to accrue. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (3) Written evidence in support of an application under the 1920 Act must also state that the judgment is not a judgment –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (a) which under section 9 of that Act may not be ordered to be registered; or

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (b) to which section 5 of the Protection of Trading Interests Act 1980 applies 7 . [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (4) Written evidence in support of an application under the 1933 Act must also –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (a) state that the judgment is a money judgment;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (b) confirm that it can be enforced by execution in the State of origin;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (c) confirm that the registration could not be set aside under section 4 of that Act;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (d) confirm that the judgment is not a judgment to which section 5 of the Protection of Trading Interests Act 1980 applies;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (e) where the judgment contains different provisions, some but not all of which can be registered for enforcement, set out those provisions in respect of which it is sought to register the judgment; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (f) be accompanied by any further evidence as to –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (i) the enforceability of the judgment in the State of origin, and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (ii) the law of that State under which any interest has become due under the judgment,

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] which may be required under the relevant Order in Council extending Part I of the 1933 Act to that State. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (5) Written evidence in support of an application under the 1982 Act must also exhibit –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (a) documents which show that, under the law of the State of origin, the judgment is enforceable on the judgment debtor and has been served;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (b) in the case of a judgment in default, a document which establishes that the party in default was served with the document instituting the proceedings or with an equivalent document; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (c) where appropriate, a document showing that the judgment creditor is in receipt of legal aid in the State of origin. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (6) Written evidence in support of an application under section 4B of the 1982 Act (registration and enforcement of judgments under the 2005 Hague Convention) must also—

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (a) confirm that the judgment—

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (i) meets the condition in Article 8(3) of the 2005 Hague Convention;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (ii) otherwise meets the requirements for recognition or enforcement under the 2005 Hague Convention; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (b) include any other evidence required by Article 13 of the 2005 Hague Convention. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (7) Written evidence in support of an application under section 4C of the 1982 Act (registration and enforcement of judgments under the 2019 Hague Convention) must also—

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (a) confirm that the judgment—

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (i) meets the condition in Article 4(3) of the 2019 Hague Convention;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (ii) meets at least one condition in Article 5 or 6 of the 2019 Hague Convention; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (iii) otherwise meets the requirements for recognition or enforcement under the 2019 Hague Convention; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.4] (b) include any other evidence required by Article 12 of the 2019 Hague Convention. ## Security for costs

## 74.5

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.5] (1) Subject to paragraphs (2) and (3), section VI of Part 25 applies to an application for security for the costs of –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.5] (a) the application for registration; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.5] (b) any proceedings brought to set aside the registration,

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.5] as if the judgment creditor were a claimant. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.5] (2) A judgment creditor making an application under the 1982 Act  may not be required to give security solely on the ground that he is resident out of the jurisdiction. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.5] (3) Paragraph (1) does not apply to an application under the 1933 Act where the relevant Order in Council otherwise provides. ## Registration orders

## 74.6

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.6] (1) An order granting permission to register a judgment (‘a registration order’) must be drawn up by the judgment creditor and served on the judgment debtor –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.6] (a) by delivering it to the judgment debtor personally;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.6] (b) by any of the methods of service permitted under the Companies Act 2006; or

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.6] (c) in such other manner as the court may direct. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.6] (2) Permission is not required to serve a registration order out of the jurisdiction, and rules 6.40, 6.42, 6.43 and 6.46 apply to such an order as they apply to a claim form. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.6] (3) A registration order must state –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.6] (a) full particulars of the judgment registered;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.6] (b) the name of the judgment creditor and his address for service within the jurisdiction;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.6] (c) the right of the judgment debtor in the case of registration following an application under the 1920 Act, the 1933 Act or the 1982 Act, to apply to have the registration set aside;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.6] (d) the period within which such an application may be made; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.6] (e) that no measures of enforcement will be taken before the end of that period, other than measures ordered by the court to preserve the property of the judgment debtor. ## Applications to set aside registration order or decision

## 74.7

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.7] (1) An application to set aside a decision on a registration application under the 1920 Act, the 1933 Act or the 1982 Act must be made within the period set out in the registration order or decision. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.7] (2) The court may extend that period; but an application for such an extension must be made before the end of the period as originally fixed or as subsequently extended. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.7] (3) The court hearing the application may order any issue between the judgment creditor and the judgment debtor to be tried. ## 74.8 Omitted

## Enforcement

## 74.9

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.9] (1)  Omitted

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.9] (2) No steps may be taken to enforce the judgment—

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.9] (a) before the end of the period specified in accordance with rule 74.6(3)(d), or that period as extended by the court; or

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.9] (b) where there is an application under rule 74.7, until the application has been determined. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.9] (3) Any party wishing to enforce a judgment  must file evidence of the service on the judgment debtor of—

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.9] (a) the registration order; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.9] (b) any other relevant order of the court. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.9] (4) Nothing in this rule prevents the court from making orders to preserve the property of the judgment debtor pending final determination of any issue relating to the enforcement of the judgment. ## Recognition

## 74.10

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.10] (1) Registration of a judgment on an application made under section 4B or 4C of the 1982 Act serves as a decision that the judgment is recognised for the purposes of the 2005 Hague Convention or the 2019 Hague Convention, respectively. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.10] (2) An application for registration of a judgment made under section 4B or 4C of the 1982 Act for the purposes of recognition is governed by the same rules as an application for registration of a judgment for the purposes of recognition and enforcement, except that rule 74.4(5)(a) and (c) do not apply. ## Authentic instruments and court settlements

## 74.11

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.11] The rules governing the registration of judgments under the 1982 Act apply as appropriate and with any necessary modifications for the enforcement of court settlements which are subject to article 12 of the 2005 Hague Convention or article 11 of the 2019 Hague Convention. ## II  ENFORCEMENT IN FOREIGN COUNTRIES OF JUDGMENTS OF THE HIGH COURT AND THE COUNTY COURT

## Application for a certified copy of a judgment

## 74.12

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.12] (1) This Section applies to applications –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.12] (a) to the High Court under section 10 of the 1920 Act;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.12] (b) to the High Court or to the County Court under section 10 of the 1933 Act; or

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.12] (c) to the High Court or to the County Court under section 12 of the 1982 Act

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.12] (2) A judgment creditor who wishes to enforce in a foreign country a judgment obtained in the High Court or in the County Court must apply for a certified copy of the judgment. [PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.12] (3) The application may be made without notice. ## Evidence in support

## 74.13

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.13] (1) The application must be supported by written evidence exhibiting copies of –

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.13] (a) the claim form in the proceedings in which judgment was given;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.13] (b) evidence that it was served on the defendant;

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.13] (c) the statements of case; and

[PART 74 – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS IN DIFFERENT JURISDICTIONS > 74.13] (d) where relevant, a document showing that for those proceedings the applicant was an assisted person or an LSC funded client, as defined in rule 43.2(1)(h) and (i).
